questions.question:
What is the time complexity of a Binary Search algorithm in the worst case?
a. O(n)
b. O(log n)
c. O(n²)
d. O(1)
questions.explanation: Binary Search repeatedly halves the search space, giving O(log n) worst-case time complexity.

questions.question:
Binary Search can be categorized into which of the following?
a) Graph algorithm
b) Divide and conquer
c) Greedy algorithm
d) Dynamic programming
questions.explanation: Binary Search divides the sorted array into halves and searches the relevant half — a classic Divide and Conquer approach.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of binary search with iteration?
a) O(n log n)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n²)
questions.explanation: Iterative Binary Search halves the search range each step, giving O(log n) time complexity.

questions.question:
Time complexity of worst case for Linear Search is ________.
a) O(1)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n²)
questions.explanation: In the worst case, Linear Search scans every element — the target is either the last element or not present — giving O(n).

questions.question:
Which of the following has search efficiency of O(1)?
a) Tree
b) Heap
c) Hash Table
d) Linked-List
questions.explanation: Hash Tables provide O(1) average-case search time using a hash function to directly compute the storage location.

questions.question:
If several elements are competing for the same bucket in the hash table, what is it called?
a) Diffusion
b) Replication
c) Collision
d) Duplication
questions.explanation: When multiple keys map to the same hash table slot/bucket, it is called a collision — resolved using techniques like chaining or probing.

questions.question:
Which of the following hashing collision resolution techniques uses a linked list to resolve collisions?
a. Linear Probing
b. Quadratic Probing
c. Double Hashing
d. Chaining
questions.explanation: Chaining maintains a linked list at each hash table slot — all elements that hash to the same index are stored in that list.

questions.question:
What is a hash table?
a) A structure that maps values to keys
b) A structure that maps keys to values
c) A structure used for storage
d) A structure used to implement stack and queue

options.A: A structure that maps values to keys
options.B: A structure that maps keys to values
options.D: A structure used to implement stack and queue

questions.explanation: A hash table maps keys to values using a hash function to compute an index — enabling fast O(1) average lookup.

questions.question:
The following numbers are inserted into an empty binary search tree in the given order: 10, 1, 3, 5, 15, 12, 16. What is the number of leaf nodes of the binary search tree?
a) 3
b) 4
c) 5
d) 6
questions.explanation: After inserting 10,1,3,5,15,12,16 into BST: leaf nodes are 5, 12, and 16 — giving 3 leaf nodes.

questions.question:
A binary tree is balanced if the difference of height between left and right sub-tree is not more than ________.
a) 0
b) 1
c) 2
d) 3
questions.explanation: An AVL tree (height-balanced BST) maintains the balance factor — the height difference between left and right subtrees — to at most 1.

questions.question:
What is another name of height balanced binary search tree?
a) Red-Black Tree
b) AVL Tree
c) B-Tree
d) Splay Tree
questions.explanation: AVL Tree (Adelson-Velsky and Landis Tree) is the classic height-balanced BST where balance factor at every node is -1, 0, or +1.

questions.question:
Balance factor of AVL tree is ________.
a) height(left subtree) - height(right subtree)
b) height(right subtree) - height(left subtree)
c) height(left subtree) + height(right subtree)
d) height(left subtree) × height(right subtree)
questions.explanation: Balance Factor = height(left subtree) - height(right subtree). For AVL tree this value must be -1, 0, or +1 at every node.

questions.question:
The process where two rotations are required to balance a tree is called ________.
a) Single rotation
b) Double rotation
c) Triple rotation
d) AVL rotation
questions.explanation: Double rotation (Left-Right or Right-Left) is needed when a single rotation is insufficient to restore the AVL balance property.

questions.question:
Given an array arr = {45, 77, 89, 90, 94, 99, 100} and key = 99; what are the mid values (corresponding array elements) in the first and second levels of recursion?
a) 90 and 99
b) 90 and 94
c) 89 and 99
d) 89 and 94
questions.explanation: First mid = index 3 → 90 (key 99 > 90, search right). Second mid = index 5 → 99 (found). Mid values are 90 and 99.

questions.question:
Worst case for linear search is ________.
a) O(1)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n²)
questions.explanation: Linear Search worst case is O(n) — the element is either the last one or not present, requiring a full scan.

What is the worst-case time complexity of searching in a Binary Search Tree (BST)?
a) O(1)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n log n)
questions.explanation: In the worst case (skewed BST), all nodes form a linear chain — search degrades to O(n), same as linear search.

questions.question:
Which of the following balanced BST guarantees O(log n) search, insert, and delete operations?
a) Unbalanced BST
b) AVL Tree
c) Linked List
d) Array
questions.explanation: AVL Tree maintains height balance at all times, guaranteeing O(log n) for search, insert, and delete operations.

questions.question:
In Linear Probing collision resolution, if a slot is occupied, the next slot is probed using which formula?
a) (h(k) + i²) mod m
b) (h(k) + i) mod m
c) (h1(k) + i × h2(k)) mod m
d) (h(k) × i) mod m
questions.explanation: Linear Probing uses (h(k) + i) mod m — probing consecutive slots linearly until an empty slot is found.

questions.question:
Symbol tables in compilers are most efficiently implemented using which data structure?
a) Array
b) Linked List
c) Hash Table
d) Stack
questions.explanation: Hash Tables are used in compilers for symbol tables — they provide O(1) average-case lookup for variable and function name resolution.

a) Linear Probing
b) Quadratic Probing
c) Double Hashing
d) Chaining
questions.explanation: Double Hashing uses two hash functions: probe sequence is (h1(k) + i × h2(k)) mod m — reducing clustering better than linear probing.
